key_insight: NeuroCBIR uses VAE plus contrastive-learning embeddings to retrieve structurally similar whole-brain or region-specific MRI scans quickly and accurately.
clinical_relevance: It could help clinicians and researchers find comparable brain MRIs for diagnosis support, prognosis, and treatment planning, especially when region-level similarity matters.
method: Extracts 103 cortical and subcortical regions from 3D T1w MRI.
Learns scan embeddings with a variational autoencoder plus contrastive learning.
Uses fast similarity search for whole-brain and region-specific retrieval.
evidence_signal: The system achieved very high re-identification performance across datasets and acquisition conditions, with mAP@5 of at least 98.4%, and embedding extraction took about 18.7 seconds per scan on a 4-core CPU.
watch_item: Although promising, the zero-shot age and pathology results are not task-trained validation, so clinical deployment would still need careful external testing and workflow integration.
paper_title: NeuroCBIR: A Fast and Accurate Image Retrieval System for Whole-Brain and Region-Specific MRI
